summary_zh: 學會在談判時用 Why don't we／How about／I'd suggest 提出建議，並用籌碼爭取更好的續約條件。

vocab.definition: the act of extending a contract for another period
vocab.example: Our contract with the cloud provider is up for renewal in December.
vocab.example_zh: 我們和雲端廠商的合約十二月要續約。

vocab.definition: a sudden, large increase in price
vocab.example: Nobody on the team was happy about the 15% price hike.
vocab.example_zh: 團隊裡沒有人對漲價 15% 感到開心。

vocab.definition: something that gives you power or an advantage in a negotiation
vocab.example: Two cheaper quotes gave us real leverage in the meeting.
vocab.example_zh: 兩份比較便宜的報價讓我們在會議上有了真正的籌碼。

vocab.definition: money taken off your bill when a supplier fails to keep its promises
vocab.example: We received a service credit after the long outage.
vocab.example_zh: 那次長時間的服務中斷之後，我們拿到了服務補償金。

vocab.definition: to fix a price or deal so that it cannot change later
vocab.example: Let's lock in this rate before it goes up again.
vocab.example_zh: 趁價格還沒再漲，我們先把這個費率鎖定吧。

vocab.definition: to refuse to continue with a deal or negotiation
vocab.example: If they won't lower the price, we're ready to walk away.
vocab.example_zh: 如果他們不降價，我們準備放棄這筆交易。

vocab.definition: to reach a compromise by giving up part of what you want
vocab.example: They asked for 10% and we offered 2%, so we agreed to meet them halfway at 6%.
vocab.example_zh: 他們要 10%，我們開 2%，所以我們同意各退一步，定在 6%。

vocab.definition: to add something extra to make an offer more attractive
vocab.example: The vendor offered free training to sweeten the deal.
vocab.example_zh: 廠商加碼提供免費訓練，讓條件更吸引人。

reading.title: Renewal Season
paragraphs: Every November, Mia Chen's team at Harbor Logistics renews its contract with CloudPeak, the company that hosts their delivery-tracking software. This year, the email from CloudPeak's account manager arrived with a 15% price hike. Mia's first reaction was to escalate it straight to her boss, but in the end she decided to prepare for the call herself.

She had more leverage than she had expected. In September, a six-hour outage had stopped drivers from updating their deliveries, and CloudPeak had missed the response time promised in the contract. That should have earned Harbor a service credit, but nobody had ever claimed it. Mia also knew that two competitors had offered similar plans for less.

On the call, she didn't threaten to walk away. "Why don't we start with September?" she said. "Before we talk about the new price, I'd suggest that we settle the credit you owe us." The account manager agreed, and the conversation became much calmer. Mia then suggested a longer renewal if CloudPeak would lock in a smaller increase. CloudPeak came back with a two-year deal at 6% instead of 15%, and, to sweeten the deal, it let Harbor's unused support hours carry over to next year.
Later, Mia's boss asked why she hadn't simply accepted the first offer. "They were willing to meet us halfway," she said, "but only after they saw that we'd done our homework."

questions.q: Why was Mia in a strong position before the call?
options: CloudPeak had broken a promise, and other companies offered similar plans for less.
Her boss had already agreed to cancel the contract.
CloudPeak had offered her a discount in September.
Harbor Logistics had never had any problems with the software.
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：CloudPeak 九月沒做到合約承諾的回應時間（six-hour outage… missed the response time），而且 two competitors had offered similar plans for less，這就是她的籌碼。

questions.q: What did Harbor get in the end?
options: A two-year contract with a 6% increase and unused support hours carried over
A one-year contract at last year's price
A 15% increase but a free year of support
No increase at all and a new account manager
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：CloudPeak came back with a two-year deal at 6% instead of 15%，還讓沒用完的支援時數 carry over to next year。

questions.q: What does Mia's last comment suggest about her approach?
options: Showing that she was well prepared made the vendor willing to compromise.
She believes vendors only respond to threats.
She wishes she had escalated the problem to her boss.
She thinks the first offer was actually fair.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：她說對方願意各退一步，but only after they saw that we'd done our homework——準備充分才讓對方願意讓步。第三段也提到她 didn't threaten to walk away，所以不是靠威脅。

grammar.point: Making suggestions: Why don't we… / I'd suggest that…
grammar.point_zh: 提出建議：Why don't we… / I'd suggest that…

guide.key_zh: Why don't we＋原形；How about／suggest＋V-ing；suggest that＋人＋原形。

uses.signal: Let's + V 意思相近，但比較直接
uses.note_zh: 不是在問為什麼，是友善的提議

uses.label_zh: 後面沒有人，直接提一個動作

uses.note_zh: 主詞是 she／he 也不加 s

mistakes.wrong: I'd suggest to lock in the price.
mistakes.right: I'd suggest locking in the price.
mistakes.why_zh: suggest 後面直接接動作要用 V-ing，不接 to V

mistakes.wrong: I'd suggest that he calls them today.
mistakes.right: I'd suggest that he call them today.
mistakes.why_zh: 美式英文 that 子句裡用原形，he 也不加 s（英式口語有人說 calls，但考試和美式寫作用 call）

mistakes.wrong: How about ask for a discount?
mistakes.right: How about asking for a discount?

examples.en: Why don't we start with the outage in September?
examples.zh: 我們要不要先從九月那次服務中斷談起？

examples.en: I'd suggest asking two other vendors for quotes.
examples.zh: 我建議向另外兩家廠商要報價。

examples.en: I'd suggest that Mia lead the call on Friday.
examples.zh: 我建議星期五的電話由 Mia 主談。

exercises.q: Why don't we ___ (ask) them for a service credit first?
exercises.explain_zh: Why don't we 後面接原形動詞 ask。

exercises.q: I'd suggest ___ (lock) in the current rate for two years.
exercises.explain_zh: suggest 後面沒有人、直接接動作時用 V-ing：locking，不是 to lock。也可以說 suggest (that) we lock。

exercises.q: How about ___ (offer) them a longer contract?
I'd suggest that our manager ___ (join) the next call.
exercises.explain_zh: suggest that + 人 + 原形：主詞 our manager 是單數也不加 s，用 join（英式也常說 should join）。

exercises.q: The vendor wants 15% more. I'd suggest ___ two other quotes before we reply.
options: getting
to get
get
got
exercises.explain_zh: suggest 後面直接接動作用 V-ing：getting。suggest 不接 to V，也不能直接接原形或過去式。

exercises.q: ___ we push the renewal call to Friday? Nobody has read the contract yet.
options: Why don't
Why won't
Why didn't
Why aren't
exercises.explain_zh: Why don't we + 原形 是友善的提議（我們要不要…）；其他選項是在真的問原因，意思不通。

listening.title: The renewal call

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Hi Rachel, thanks for making time. Sorry if I sound a bit rough. My allergies have flared up, and I've been taking over-the-counter meds all week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Oh no, I hope you feel better soon. So, you've had a chance to look at our renewal proposal?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: I have. Honestly, a twelve percent price hike is going to be hard to sell internally.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: I understand. Our own costs have gone up a lot this year.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Sure. Look, we've been using your platform for five years, and it's worked well for us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: But why don't we look at what we got last year first? The outage in March took two days to fix.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: That's fair. I can check whether you're owed a service credit.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Thanks. And I'd suggest that we sign for three years instead of one, if the price works for both of us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: A three-year renewal would definitely help. How about locking in an eight percent increase?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Could you meet us halfway at six? Then I can get it approved this week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Let me talk to my manager. I can't promise anything, but I think we can work with that.

questions.q: Why does Daniel say he sounds rough?
options: His allergies have flared up.
He has just come back from a long flight.
He was up late reading the contract.
He has lost his voice after a presentation.
questions.explain_zh: Daniel 一開始就說 My allergies have flared up，所以在吃成藥。

questions.q: What does Daniel offer in exchange for a smaller increase?
options: A three-year contract
Paying the whole year in advance
Giving up the service credit
Moving to a cheaper plan
questions.explain_zh: Daniel：I'd suggest that we sign for three years instead of one, if the price works for both of us。

questions.q: What will most likely happen next?
options: Rachel will ask her manager about a 6% increase.
Rachel will agree to 6% before the call ends.
Daniel will cancel the contract.
Daniel will accept the 8% increase.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：Rachel 最後說 Let me talk to my manager… I think we can work with that，表示她要回去跟主管談 6%，還沒有當場答應。

dictation: Why don't we look at what we got last year first?
We've been using your platform for five years, and it's worked well for us.
I'd suggest that we sign for three years instead of one, if the price works for both of us.

shadowing: Why don't we start with the outage in September?
I'd suggest locking in the current rate for two years.
Could you meet us halfway at six percent?
I'd suggest that our manager join the next call.

prompts.question: A vendor wants to raise its price by 10%. Make one suggestion to your team in one or two sentences.
prompts.question_zh: 廠商要漲價 10%。用一兩句話向團隊提出一個建議。
prompts.sample: Why don't we ask two other vendors for quotes first? I'd suggest that we reply only after we see their numbers.

prompts.question: Give a one-sentence progress update on a deal or project you are working on.
prompts.question_zh: 用一句話報告你手上一個案子或專案的進度。
prompts.sample: So far, we've agreed on the price, but we haven't signed the renewal yet.

writing.task: Your company's software vendor has announced a 12% price hike. Write a short email to your manager in three short paragraphs: (1) the problem, (2) what you've done so far, and (3) your suggested next step. End every sentence with a full stop instead of joining sentences with commas.
writing.task_zh: 公司的軟體廠商宣布漲價 12%。寫一封短信給主管，分三小段：(1) 問題是什麼；(2) 你目前做了什麼；(3) 你建議的下一步。每句用句號結束，不要用逗號把句子串在一起。
writing.sample:
Hi Karen,

CloudPeak has sent over our renewal terms, and they include a 12% price hike. At a glance, the new plan looks the same as the old one. That makes the increase hard to justify.

So far, I've compared two other vendors, and both have offered similar plans for less. I've also checked our records. Their outage in September kept our drivers offline for six hours, so they owe us a service credit.

I'd suggest that we ask for the credit before we discuss the price. Why don't we also offer a two-year contract if they lock in a smaller increase? I can set up the call for Friday.

Thanks,
Daniel
checklist_zh: 有沒有分成三小段：問題、目前做了什麼、下一步
Why don't we 接原形；I'd suggest 接 V-ing 或 that + 人 + 原形
so far 後面用現在完成式（I've compared、have offered）
每句用句號結束，沒有用逗號硬接句子

reading.title: The Buyer Who Can Say No
paragraphs: Ask any seasoned procurement manager what the most powerful word in a negotiation is, and many will tell you it's "no." Not a slammed-door no, but a calm, well-timed one that signals you have options. The trouble is that most buyers only start looking at their options after the vendor has already set the terms, and by then they're on the back foot.

Take a mid-sized retailer I advised last spring. Its payment provider had quietly raised fees twice in eighteen months, and the finance team had simply absorbed the increases, assuming that switching would be too disruptive. When we finally ran the numbers, the "disruption" turned out to be about three weeks of testing, at a fraction of what the extra fees were costing them every quarter.

Armed with that figure, the retailer didn't storm into the renewal meeting with ultimatums. Instead, its head of finance laid out the cost of staying and the cost of leaving side by side, and politely asked the provider to explain why the first number should be the larger one. The room went quiet, and for once nobody on the provider's side had a ready answer. Within a week, the provider had rolled back its most recent increase and thrown in a dedicated support contact.

The lesson here isn't that you should bluff. Vendors deal with bluffers every day, and most of them can spot one a mile away. The lesson is that credibility comes from homework: knowing your alternatives, knowing what a switch would really involve in time and money, and being genuinely prepared to act on that knowledge. Paradoxically, the buyers who are most willing to walk away are the ones who rarely have to.

questions.q: Why had the retailer kept paying the higher fees?
options: It assumed that changing providers would cause too much disruption.
Its contract made it impossible to switch.
The finance team didn't notice the increases.
The provider had offered better support in return.
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：the finance team had simply absorbed the increases, assuming that switching would be too disruptive。

questions.q: Why did the room most likely go quiet?
options: The provider could not easily justify charging more than it would cost the retailer to leave.
The head of finance had threatened to cancel the contract immediately.
The provider was offended by the retailer's rude tone.
Nobody in the meeting understood the figures.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：財務主管把留下和離開的成本並排，問對方為什麼留下的成本應該比較高；對方答不出來，所以一片安靜。文中說他們沒有下最後通牒（didn't storm in with ultimatums），態度也是 politely。

questions.q: What does the writer mean in the last sentence?
options: Buyers who are truly ready to leave usually get what they want without leaving.
Buyers should change suppliers as often as possible.
Buyers who walk away often regret it later.
Buyers should pretend they have other options even when they don't.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：真正準備好離開的買方，對方會讓步，所以很少真的需要離開。作者前面也說 The lesson here isn't that you should bluff，所以不是叫你假裝有選擇。

listening.title: Before the vendor joins

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Nadia
lines.text: Okay, so before Lisa joins, have you actually read their counteroffer?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Owen
lines.text: Skimmed it. They've dropped from twelve to nine percent, which, honestly—

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Nadia
lines.text: Which is still way too much, yeah. They're acting like the March outage never happened.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Owen
lines.text: Right, and that's our ace in the hole, isn't it? I mean, they blew through the SLA twice.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Nadia
lines.text: Exactly. So here's what I'm thinking. We open with the credits, not the price.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Owen
lines.text: Hmm. Won't that put them on the defensive? If we come in swinging—

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Nadia
lines.text: We don't come in swinging. We just put the numbers on the table and let them do the math.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Owen
lines.text: Fair enough. And if they dig their heels in?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Nadia
lines.text: Then I'd suggest we mention, very casually, that we've had a demo from Brightline.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Owen
lines.text: Have we, though? I thought that got pushed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Nadia
lines.text: It's on Thursday. So technically, by the time they sign anything, it'll be true.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Owen
lines.text: Ha! Sneaky. Okay, but let's not show our hand too early.

questions.q: How does Nadia want to start the meeting?
options: By talking about the credits the vendor owes them
By rejecting the nine percent offer outright
By announcing that they are switching to Brightline
By asking Lisa to explain the new price
questions.explain_zh: Nadia：We open with the credits, not the price。

options: That starting with the credits might make the vendor defensive
That they haven't read the counteroffer carefully enough
That the Brightline demo will be canceled
That the SLA has not been broken
questions.explain_zh: Owen：Won't that put them on the defensive? If we come in swinging… put someone on the defensive 是讓對方防衛起來、不高興。

questions.q: What can we infer about the Brightline demo?
options: It hasn't happened yet.
It went badly.
Owen ran it last week.
The vendor already knows about it.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：Owen 問 Have we, though? I thought that got pushed，Nadia 回答 It's on Thursday，by the time they sign anything, it'll be true——表示現在還沒做。

dictation: They're acting like the March outage never happened.
We open with the credits, not the price.
Let's not show our hand too early.
